result.markdown: --- title: "Session 2 — Splines" subtitle: "Piecewise-linear terms · natural cubic splines · degrees of freedom · prediction plots · splines in logistic models · Lab 2" author: "Community Medicine Workshop" format: revealjs: theme: serif css: [../assets/slide_deck.css, assets/workshop.css, assets/quiz.css] include-after-body: assets/quiz-include.html embed-resources: true slide-number: true navigation-mode: linear code-copy: true center: false transition: fade width: 1280 height: 720 fig-align: center html-math-method: plain execute: echo: true warning: false message: false fig-width: 9 fig-height: 4.6 fig-dpi: 100 --- ## Where we are ::: {.incremental} - Session 1: found curvature; simple fixes - Today: **splines**, the flexible, general tool - By the end you can: - fit a **hinge** (piecewise-linear) term - fit a **natural spline** with `ns()` and choose its **df** - draw a **prediction plot** with a CI band - test **non-linearity** in a logistic model ::: # Topic 1 — Piecewise linear {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## A hinge at age 45 ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} m_h <- lm(sbp ~ age + pmax(age - 45, 0) + bmi + salt + activity + sex + smoker, data = ncd) round(coef(m_h)[2:3], 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` age pmax(age - 45, 0) 0.272 0.288 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} c(before = coef(m_h)[["age"]], after = coef(m_h)[["age"]] + coef(m_h)[[3]]) |> round(2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` before after 0.27 0.56 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} `pmax(age - 45, 0)` is **0 below 45** and **age − 45 above it**: its coefficient is the **change in slope**. SBP rises **0.27 mmHg per year before 45** and **0.56 after**: twice as fast. Easy to **explain**, and the slopes are **directly reportable**. ::: ## Where is the knot? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} aic_k <- sapply(30:60, function(k) AIC(lm(sbp ~ age + pmax(age - k, 0) + bmi + salt + activity + sex + smoker, data = ncd))) (30:60)[which.min(aic_k)] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 45 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.warn} The data choose **45**. But a knot **picked from the data** is not free: the search is **not counted**, so CIs are **too narrow**. Prefer a knot from **subject knowledge** (e.g. a clinical cut-off), or use a **smooth** spline. ::: # Topic 2 — Natural splines {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## ns(): a smooth curve ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} m_l <- lm(sbp ~ age + bmi + salt + activity + sex + smoker, data = ncd) m_ns <- lm(sbp ~ ns(age, df = 4) + bmi + salt + activity + sex + smoker, data = ncd) anova(m_l, m_ns) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Analysis of Variance Table Model 1: sbp ~ age + bmi + salt + activity + sex + smoker Model 2: sbp ~ ns(age, df = 4) + bmi + salt + activity + sex + smoker Res.Df RSS Df Sum of Sq F Pr(>F) 1 3993 511350 2 3990 506177 3 5173.2 13.593 8.043e-09 *** --- Signif. codes: 0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - `ns(age, df = 4)` builds **4 columns** (a **basis**); knots go at **quantiles** of age - **Natural** = **linear beyond the outer knots**, so the tails behave - The 4 coefficients are **not interpretable one by one**: interpret the **curve** and **tests** - The F test against the straight line: p ≈ 8×10⁻⁹ ::: ## How many degrees of freedom? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} aic_df <- sapply(1:8, function(k) AIC(lm(sbp ~ ns(age, df = k) + bmi + salt + activity + sex + smoker, data = ncd))) round(setNames(aic_df, paste0("df", 1:8)), 0) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` df1 df2 df3 df4 df5 df6 df7 df8 30771 30735 30736 30736 30735 30735 30736 30737 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} **df = 1 is a straight line.** AIC drops by **36** at df = 2, then stays **flat**: **3 to 5 df** are plenty for age. More df just adds **wiggles** (Session 5 shows it **hurts prediction**). Rule of thumb: **3 to 5 df** for a main predictor, fewer for small data. ::: ## A prediction plot ::: {.cell output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} grid <- data.frame(age = 18:80, bmi = mean(ncd$bmi), salt = mean(ncd$salt), activity = mean(ncd$activity), sex = factor("Male", levels = levels(ncd$sex)), smoker = 0) pr <- predict(m_ns, newdata = grid, se.fit = TRUE) grid |> mutate(fit = pr$fit, lo = fit - 1.96 * pr$se.fit, hi = fit + 1.96 * pr$se.fit) |> ggplot(aes(age, fit)) + geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.25, fill = col_blue) + geom_line(linewidth = 1.2, colour = col_blue) + labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Predicted SBP (mmHg)") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](s2_splines_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png){width=900} ::: ::: ::: {.key} **Predicted SBP with a 95% band**, other variables held at **typical values** (mean BMI, salt, activity; man; non-smoker). The **plot is the result**: report it instead of the coefficients. ::: # Topic 3 — Splines for binary outcomes {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## BMI and CVD risk ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} g_ns <- glm(cvd10 ~ age + ns(bmi, 4) + sex + smoker, data = ncd, family = binomial) g_l <- glm(cvd10 ~ age + bmi + sex + smoker, data = ncd, family = binomial) anova(g_l, g_ns, test = "Chisq") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Analysis of Deviance Table Model 1: cvd10 ~ age + bmi + sex + smoker Model 2: cvd10 ~ age + ns(bmi, 4) + sex + smoker Resid. Df Resid. Dev Df Deviance Pr(>Chi) 1 3995 2271.9 2 3992 2037.0 3 234.92 < 2.2e-16 *** --- Signif. codes: 0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} gb <- data.frame(bmi = seq(15, 40, 0.5), age = 50, sex = factor("Male", levels = levels(ncd$sex)), smoker = 0) gb$p <- predict(g_ns, newdata = gb, type = "response") ggplot(gb, aes(bmi, p)) + geom_line(linewidth = 1.2, colour = col_red) + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + labs(x = "BMI", y = "10-year CVD risk") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](s2_splines_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-8-1.png){width=900} ::: ::: ::: {.key} Likelihood-ratio test: deviance drop **235 on 3 df**, so a straight line is **not enough**. The curve is **U-shaped**: lowest near **BMI 24 to 25**, high for low BMI, much higher for **obesity**. ::: ## Cautions ::: {.warn} - Predictions **outside the data range** are **extrapolation** (the natural spline continues in a straight line) - A spline with **too many df** fits **noise** (Session 5) - Put the spline **inside the model** with the other predictors, then predict **holding them fixed** ::: ## 🔧 Switch to R — Lab 2 {.lab-slide background-color="#1565c0"} ::: {.lab-box} **File:** `curves-workshop/labs/lab2_splines.R` - hinge term, slopes and knot search - natural spline, df choice, prediction plot - spline for BMI in a logistic model ::: **Time:** 40 minutes · answer the Q questions in the comments ## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="k2q1" data-type="mcq" data-hash="owt86i.ucbdqz" data-show="VGhlIGNoYW5nZSBpbiBzbG9wZSBhZnRlciBhZ2UgNDUgY29tcGFyZWQgd2l0aCB0aGUgc2xv cGUgYmVmb3Jl" data-explain="VGhlIGhpbmdlIGlzIHplcm8gdW50aWwgYWdlIDQ1LCBzbyBpdHMgY29lZmZpY2llbnQgaXMg dGhlIGV4dHJhIHNsb3BlIGFmdGVyIHRoZSBrbm90LiBUaGUgc2xvcGUgYWZ0ZXIgaXMgdGhl IHN1bSBvZiB0aGUgdHdvIGNvZWZmaWNpZW50cyAoMC4yNyArIDAuMjkpLg=="} In a model with age + pmax(age - 45, 0), the coefficient of the hinge term is 0.29. What does it estimate? - The mean SBP of the adults who are older than 45 years in the survey - The slope of SBP in the adults who are older than 45 years of age - The age at which SBP starts to rise among the adults in the survey - The change in slope after age 45 compared with the slope before ::: ## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="k2q2" data-type="mcq" data-hash="owtlf4.ucbs89" data-show="VGhlIHNlYXJjaCBpcyBub3QgY291bnRlZCwgc28gdGhlIENJcyBjb21lIG91dCB0b28gbmFy cm93" data-explain="VHJ5aW5nIG1hbnkga25vdHMgaXMgYSBmb3JtIG9mIG11bHRpcGxlIHRlc3RpbmcgdGhhdCB0 aGUgc3RhbmRhcmQgZXJyb3JzIGlnbm9yZS4gQSBrbm90IGZyb20gc3ViamVjdC1tYXR0ZXIg a25vd2xlZGdlLCBvciBhIHNtb290aCB0ZXJtLCBhdm9pZHMgdGhpcy4="} Why is picking the knot from the data (the best AIC over many knots) a problem? - The search is not counted, so the CIs come out too narrow - The model can no longer be fitted by least squares once the search is done - Knots chosen from the data bias the estimates of every other coefficient - The AIC cannot be computed for a model whose knot was found by searching ::: ## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="k2q3" data-type="mcq" data-hash="owtynu.ucc6pn" data-show="QSBzbW9vdGggY3VydmUgd2hvc2UgZm91ciBiYXNpcyBjb2VmZmljaWVudHMgYXJlIG5vdCBy ZWFkIG9uZSBieSBvbmU=" data-explain="QSBuYXR1cmFsIHNwbGluZSBpcyBhIGZsZXhpYmxlIHNtb290aCBjdXJ2ZSwgbGluZWFyIGJl eW9uZCB0aGUgb3V0ZXIga25vdHMuIEl0cyBiYXNpcyBjb2VmZmljaWVudHMgZGVwZW5kIG9u IHRoZSBjb25zdHJ1Y3Rpb24sIHNvIGludGVycHJldCB0aGUgZml0dGVkIGN1cnZlLg=="} What is the best description of ns(age, df = 4)? - Four straight segments joined at the quartiles of age in the survey data - A smooth curve whose four basis coefficients are not read one by one - A polynomial of degree four in age, in which each coefficient has a clear meaning - Four separate age effects, one for each of four fixed age groups in the data ::: ## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="k2q4" data-type="mcq" data-hash="owubwl.uccl72" data-show="QSBzbWFsbCBudW1iZXIgc3VjaCBhcyAzIG9yIDQsIHNpbmNlIG1vcmUgZmxleGliaWxpdHkg YWRkcyBub3RoaW5n" data-explain="VGhlIGZpdCBpbXByb3ZlcyBncmVhdGx5IGZyb20gMSB0byAyIGRmIGFuZCB0aGVuIHN0YXlz IGZsYXQuIEV4dHJhIGRmIGFkZCB3aWdnbGUgYW5kIHZhcmlhbmNlIHdpdGhvdXQgaW1wcm92 aW5nIHRoZSBmaXQu"} The AIC for natural splines with 1 to 8 df is 30,771 then about 30,735 from 2 df onwards. Which choice is sensible? - 8, since more flexibility gives a more correct curve for the data - 1, since a straight line is preferred to a curve whatever the AIC - No value can be justified, because AIC cannot help to choose the df - A small number such as 3 or 4, since more flexibility adds nothing ::: ## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="k2q5" data-type="mcq" data-hash="owup57.ucczoc" data-show="UHJlZGljdCBvdmVyIGEgZ3JpZCBvZiBhZ2VzIHdpdGggc2UuZml0LCB3aXRoIHRoZSBvdGhl ciB2YXJpYWJsZXMgZml4ZWQ=" data-explain="UHJlZGljdGlvbnMgY29tZSBmcm9tIGEgbmV3IGRhdGEgZ3JpZCwgd2l0aCB0aGUgb3RoZXIg Y292YXJpYXRlcyBhdCBjaG9zZW4gdmFsdWVzLCBhbmQgdGhlIGJhbmQgZnJvbSB0aGUgc3Rh bmRhcmQgZXJyb3JzIG9mIHRoZSBwcmVkaWN0aW9ucy4="} How is a prediction plot with a 95% band for a spline model built? - Predict over a grid of ages with se.fit, with the other variables fixed - Plot the fitted values of the sample against age and join the points together - Plot each spline coefficient against the age at which its knot is placed - Fit a separate model for each age in the data and plot the intercepts ::: ## Score and take-home **Your score: ** ::: {.incremental} - **Hinge** `pmax(x - k, 0)`: change in slope at a chosen knot - **`ns(x, df)`**: smooth natural spline, 3 to 5 df - Test non-linearity with **anova** (F or LR test) - **Prediction plot with a CI band** is the result - Beware **extrapolation** and too many df ::: **Next:** Session 3: generalised additive models

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
